You are evaluating a software engineering task for repository fastapi/fastapi.

Problem Statement:
🐛 Fix internal Pydantic v1 compatibility (warnings) for Python 3.14 and Pydantic 2.12.1

The Python 3.14 tests started failing with the Pydantic v.2.12.1 release, because of the combination of https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/14168 and https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/12367.

Basically we were importing Pydantic `v1` functionality even when the user had (only) Pydantic v2 installed. This was done in https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/14168 to support more easy migration from v1 to v2 by allowing mixing versions within the same app.

Here, we prevent importing any `v1` functionality by creating dummy classes for Python 3.14 / Pydantic 2.12.0 onwards, which [drops support](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/releases/tag/v2.12.0) for `v1` and emits a [warning](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/12367) when importing `v1` functionality.

The issue was that Pydantic v2.12.0+ for Python 3.14 drops support for the `pydantic.v1` compatibility layer, causing import warnings in FastAPI. To resolve this, I modified `fastapi/_compat/v1.py` to detect environments where Python $\ge$ 3.14 and Pydantic $\ge$ 2.12.0 are used. In such cases, the import of `pydantic.v1` is avoided, and the expected classes and functions are replaced with dummy implementations (a `Dummy` class and several lambda functions) to ensure that FastAPI's internal logic continues to function without crashing, while avoiding the deprecated import.

Summary of changes:
- Added `SHOULD_AVOID_V1_IMPORT` flag to `fastapi/_compat/v1.py` based on Python and Pydantic versions.
- Implemented an `elif SHOULD_AVOID_V1_IMPORT` block in `fastapi/_compat/v1.py` to provide dummy replacements for Pydantic v1 symbols.
